name: The last interglacial (Eemian)
what: A warm spell a little warmer than today; hippos lived in the Thames and the sea was 6 to 9 m higher.
why: The world as it was before the last ice age.

sources.cite: Dutton, A. et al., "Sea-level rise due to polar ice-sheet mass loss during past warm periods", Science 349, aaa4019 (2015)

name: Neanderthal-modern human mixing
what: Modern humans leaving Africa mixed with Neanderthals, most likely in western Asia.
why: Everyone outside Africa carries 1 to 2% Neanderthal DNA from this time.

sources.cite: Fu, Q. et al., "Genome sequence of a 45,000-year-old modern human from western Siberia", Nature 514, 445-449 (2014)

name: Laschamps geomagnetic excursion
what: Earth's magnetic field fell to a few percent of today's strength and flipped briefly.
why: More cosmic rays reached the ground; some argue it shaped climate and cave use, which is debated.

sources.cite: Cooper, A. et al., "A global environmental crisis 42,000 years ago", Science 371, 811-818 (2021)

name: Campanian Ignimbrite eruption
what: The Campi Flegrei volcano near Naples buried southern Italy in ash and threw tephra as far as Russia.
why: The largest eruption in Europe in 200,000 years, as Neanderthals were vanishing.

sources.cite: Giaccio, B. et al., "High-precision 14C and 40Ar/39Ar dating of the Campanian Ignimbrite (Y-5) reconciles the time-scales of climatic-cultural processes at 40 ka", Scientific Reports 7, 45940 (2017)

name: Last Glacial Maximum
what: Ice reached its greatest extent; the sea stood about 130 m lower than today.
why: The coldest stretch of the last ice age: Europe north of the Alps emptied of people and refuges filled.

sources.cite: Clark, P. U. et al., "The Last Glacial Maximum", Science 325, 710-714 (2009)

name: Meltwater pulse 1A
what: The sea rose about 14 to 18 m in roughly 350 years as the ice sheets collapsed.
why: Coasts moved inland by kilometres within a few lifetimes; the record comes from Tahiti's drowned reefs.

sources.cite: Deschamps, P. et al., "Ice-sheet collapse and sea-level rise at the Bølling warming 14,600 years ago", Nature 483, 559-564 (2012)

name: Younger Dryas
what: A sudden return to near-glacial cold in the north for about 1,200 years.
why: Some argue the cold pushed Natufian foragers toward farming.

sources.cite: Rasmussen, S. O. et al., "A new Greenland ice core chronology for the last glacial termination", Journal of Geophysical Research 111, D06102 (2006)

name: The Holocene begins
what: The ice age ends; the Greenland ice dates the start to 11,700 years ago.
why: The stable, warm climate in which farming and every civilisation began.

sources.cite: Walker, M. et al., "Formal definition and dating of the GSSP for the base of the Holocene", Journal of Quaternary Science 24, 3-17 (2009)

name: The Green Sahara (African Humid Period)
what: Monsoon rains turned the Sahara into grassland with lakes, hippos and herders; Lake Mega-Chad was as big as the Caspian.
why: When the rains failed, herders moved to the Nile, around the time Egypt began.

sources.cite: deMenocal, P. et al., "Abrupt onset and termination of the African Humid Period", Quaternary Science Reviews 19, 347-361 (2000)

name: The 8.2 kiloyear event
what: Lake Agassiz drained into the North Atlantic, and the north cooled for about 150 years.
why: A short shock to early farmers in the Near East and Europe.

sources.cite: Alley, R. B. et al., "Holocene climatic instability: a prominent, widespread event 8200 yr ago", Geology 25, 483-486 (1997)

name: Storegga Slide tsunami
what: A submarine landslide off Norway sent a tsunami across the North Sea; run-up reached 20 m in Shetland.
why: It may have drowned the last of Doggerland.

sources.cite: Weninger, B. et al., "The catastrophic final flooding of Doggerland by the Storegga Slide tsunami", Documenta Praehistorica 35, 1-24 (2008)
